subject: Post-call recap & proposed MAP gating criteria (technical evaluation milestone)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Lewis <hannah@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed MAP gating criteria (technical evaluation milestone)

Thanks again for the time today, Hannah — good conversation and helpful context on the internal success criteria. Per our call, I pulled together a concise proposal for the MAP technical evaluation milestone so we can align owners and gating criteria before we lock the formal plan. Attaching a working MAP spreadsheet (MAP_Draft_v1.xlsx) and a short eval dataset manifest.

Quick recap (from today's discovery):
- Goal: Replace in-house generative responses for patient triage assistant with a hosted/dedicated Redwood deployment that meets clinical SLAs and keeps unit cost <= target.
- Primary constraints: p95 latency must be predictable under bursty traffic; data residency for PHI; clear audit logs.
- Key internal stakeholders you named: Hannah (OB), infra lead (DevOps), procurement.

Proposed MAP — technical evaluation milestone (summary):
1) Scope: run benchmark suite for representative traffic (real-ish prompts + synthetic variations).
2) Success criteria (pass/fail gates):
   - Quality: end-to-end semantic match >= 0.85 on our clinical rubric (acceptance tests in eval_manifest).
   - Latency: p95 generation latency <= 350 ms at concurrency 8 (prefix caching enabled).
   - Cost: amortized token cost <= $0.0028/token at target QPS.
   - Reliability: no model crash or OOM for sequences up to 2k tokens across 24h soak test.
3) Model shortlist to evaluate: Llama-3-70B-q4f, Falcon-40B-Instruct, and Redwood-v1-xl (redwood-curated open variant).
4) Deliverables: benchmark results (CSV + dashboard), evaluation notebook, final recommendation and runbook for integration.
5) Owners & target dates: Marissa — bench harness & acceptance tests (complete by 2026-11-06); Rishi — cost modeling and unit economics (supporting artifacts by 2026-11-06); Connor — infra gating and test environment (provision by 2026-10-21).
6) Dependencies: access to sanitized sample prompts (you), temporary test VPC with GPU nodes (we need DevOps), and signed NDA/data addendum for PHI test vectors (procurement/legal).

Can you confirm: 1) the infra contact to provision the test VPC, and 2) whether procurement can start the data addendum draft? If that looks OK I will move the MAP sheet to the shared folder and lock the milestone dates.

Next step: I proposed a readout week of 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-13 — if we hit the owners' dates above we can share results and a recommended approach.

Attachments: MAP_Draft_v1.xlsx, eval_dataset_manifest.csv

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Sean — thanks for the recap and the clear checklist. A few clarifications from my side:
- The clinical rubric target (>=0.85) sounds reasonable, but I need to confirm with clinical ops whether the rubric maps to our pass/fail bar for triage. I expect to have confirmation by EOD Friday (2026-10-09).
- For infra provisioning: looping in infra (cc'd). We typically require an internal change request for any external VPC access; will infra let us know required params and timeline?
- Procurement: can you start a draft of the data addendum? We need to know if Redwood needs any custom DPA terms for PHI.

I also want more detail on the cost target — $0.0028/token is helpful, but can you and Rishi provide a simple proforma that maps expected monthly spend at our estimated QPS? That will help procurement and finance.

I will review the MAP_Draft_v1.xlsx and send any edits inline.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Lewis <hannah@healthgrid.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-10-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed MAP gating criteria (technical evaluation milestone)

Adding technical detail for the evaluation plan so everyone has concrete gates to react to. Keeping this focused so the MAP can be updated quickly.

Evaluation specifics (proposed):
- Dataset: ~3k representative prompts + 10k synthetic paraphrases; manifest attached (eval_dataset_manifest.csv). We'll run both deterministic and sampled decoding to exercise safety filters.
- Metrics:
  * Semantic similarity (clinical rubric): macro-F1 or normalized BLEU-like metric converted to 0-1; acceptance threshold >= 0.85.
  * Safety pass rate: 100% for red-flag triggers (no PHI leakage, no disallowed advice).
  * Latency: measure end-to-end generation from request to final token streamed, p95 <= 350 ms at concurrency 8. If using prefix caching we will also report cold vs warm p95.
  * Cost: compare per-token inference cost across models; target amortized cost <= $0.0028/token but we'll include sensitivity for QPS +/-25%.
- Model shortlist rationale:
  1) Llama-3-70B-q4f — best quality for instruction workloads in our curated runs, strong instruction-following and safety adapter support.
  2) Falcon-40B-Instruct — favorable cost/latency tradeoff on ampere-class GPUs and easy to quantize.
  3) Redwood-v1-xl — our curated open variant with tuned kernels, expected to be the lowest latency path with caching.
- Test harness: use the HG-specific branch of our eval-harness (link in MAP sheet). We'll provide a Docker image and a small benchmark job config.
- Ownership (confirm):
  * Bench harness & acceptance tests: Marissa (owner)
  * Cost proforma & sensitivity: Rishi (owner)
  * Infra provisioning & test VPC: Connor (owner)
  * Data access & legal flow: Priyom (support / coordinate with Procurement)
- Timelines: bench runs + initial readout target 2026-11-06; final recommendation and runbook by 2026-11-12.

If this looks good I will update MAP_Draft_v1.xlsx with the gate definitions and add a worksheet for raw results. Also attaching a short cost_model_proforma.pdf (sample) to show the format Rishi will use.

On dependencies: to avoid delays we can run an initial dry-run with sanitized synthetic prompts while procurement/legal complete the addendum. That will surface infra issues early.

Marissa Cole
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
